security_audit.summary: All 82 static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, instructional prose, or the local validator shell syntax. The validator parses a supplied file with quoted values and does not evaluate its contents. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed materials.

remediation.issue: Static scanners misclassify Markdown backticks and documentation examples as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Use scanner rules that distinguish fenced or inline Markdown code from executable shell content.

remediation.issue: The validator accepts a user-provided file path.
remediation.suggestion: Keep path variables quoted and consider adding -- before file operands where supported.

content.value_statement: Plugin agents can trigger poorly or receive excessive tool access. This skill provides templates and guidance for focused agents with clear behavior.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Markdown and YAML structure for plugin agent files.
Defines names, descriptions, models, colors, and optional tool restrictions.
Provides triggering examples for agent descriptions.
Offers system prompt structure and quality guidance.
Shows manual and AI-assisted agent creation workflows.
Includes a shell validator for agent file structure.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not a running agent implementation.
It does not test agent behavior in every Claude Code version.
The validator checks basic structure and does not perform a full security review.
Tool availability depends on the host environment and plugin configuration.

use_cases.title: Create a first plugin agent
use_cases.description: Build a focused agent file with required frontmatter and a structured prompt.

use_cases.title: Improve agent triggering
use_cases.description: Add concrete descriptions and examples so the correct agent is selected for user requests.

use_cases.title: Review agent permissions
use_cases.description: Choose the smallest practical tool set for analysis, generation, or testing work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple review agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Claude Code agent that reviews TypeScript files. Include a name, triggering description, focused tools, and a short system prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Add triggering examples
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this agent description with three concrete triggering examples. Explain when the agent should not run: [paste description].

prompt_templates.title: Apply least privilege
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the minimum Claude Code tools for an agent that analyzes code and reports findings without editing files. Explain each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Design a specialized agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a plugin agent for [domain]. Define boundaries, a repeatable process, edge cases, output expectations, and safe tool permissions.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that checks API documentation for missing examples.
output: A specific agent name and trigger description.
A system prompt with review steps and a report format.

output_examples.input: Which tools should a test-planning agent receive?
output: A least-privilege recommendation for reading files and searching code.
An explanation of when a shell tool is unnecessary.

best_practices: Use specific triggering conditions and several realistic examples.
Grant only the tools required for the agent task.
Define responsibilities, process steps, edge cases, and output expectations.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that overlap with unrelated agents.
Do not grant full tool access when read-only tools are sufficient.
Do not omit testing for triggering behavior and edge cases.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps you create and document Claude Code plugin agents.

faq.question: Does it create agents automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance, templates, and validation. You create or generate the final agent file.

faq.question: Why are triggering examples important?
faq.answer: Examples clarify when Claude Code should select an agent for a request.

faq.question: Which model should an agent use?
faq.answer: Use inherit by default. Choose another model only when the task requires it.

faq.question: Can I restrict agent tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends choosing the minimum tool set needed for the task.

faq.question: What does the validator check?
faq.answer: It checks frontmatter, selected fields, system prompt presence, and basic format rules.
